question: When one frozen Eevee Render Result is saved as both scene-linear RGBA32 float OpenEXR and display-referred RGBA8 PNG, in which output domain does strict cross-process variation first remain observable?

evidenceBasis.acceptedOperationalBoundary: One background render call can save the same Render Result as PNG RGBA8 and ZIP OpenEXR RGBA32; bundled OIIO decodes the EXR as 960x540 RGBA float. Direct Render Result.pixels access was empty and is excluded.

design.type: same-Render-Result dual-file localization with three fresh-process replicates per sentinel

outputs.colorDomain: scene-linear ACEScg under the pinned B02 BuildPlan/OCIO contract

exactGate.perFormat: All 12 sentinel frames must be exact in all A-B, A-C and B-C pairs: 36/36.

decisionRule.DISPLAY_PNG_PATH_SUPPORT: EXR32_SCENE_LINEAR is exact 36/36 and PNG8_DISPLAY is non-exact, with a valid experiment.
decisionRule.PRE_PNG_VARIATION_SUPPORT: Both EXR32_SCENE_LINEAR and PNG8_DISPLAY are non-exact, with a valid experiment.
decisionRule.PNG_QUANTIZATION_MASKS_FLOAT_VARIATION: EXR32_SCENE_LINEAR is non-exact and PNG8_DISPLAY is exact 36/36, with a valid experiment.
decisionRule.VARIATION_NOT_REPRODUCED: Both formats are exact 36/36, with a valid experiment.
decisionRule.INVALID_EXPERIMENT: Any frozen identity, process, one-render/two-save, format/layout, image, binding, count or negative-case gate fails.

requiredNegativeCases: render operator count differs from one
PNG or EXR partner is missing
PNG or EXR bytes are mutated
comparison is not bound to both file and manifest hashes
explicitNonClaims: The experiment does not directly read Blender's in-memory pixel buffer; it compares two files saved from the same Render Result.
A non-exact EXR localizes variation to at or before the scene-linear EXR save boundary, not to a specific shader, sample reducer, driver or GPU race.
An exact EXR and non-exact PNG would support the display/output path under this profile but would not prove which color-transform or quantization operation is causal.
Three replicates can falsify strict determinism but cannot estimate a stable mismatch probability.
No perceptual tolerance is selected and near-equality remains non-exact.
The result applies to Blender 5.2 Eevee on this machine and does not establish Cycles, multilayer EXR, AOV or cross-device reproducibility.
